assignments.title: Primary Source Report: Roosevelt and the Wannsee Protocol
assignments.html:
PRIMARY SOURCE REPORT
Roosevelt and the Wannsee Protocol
World War II and the Holocaust
16 points · text entry
✹ ✦ ✹
Before you start

Finish both lessons and read both sources first. Your notes from each page are kept in My Notebook, the button inside the page, so open it before you write. Then write your answers and submit them in this assignment.

QUESTIONS
1. President Roosevelt addressed Congress on December 8, 1941. The record of the Wannsee meeting was written in January 1942. For each document, say who is speaking, who the intended audience is, and what the speakers wanted their audience to do or to understand. How might those differences change what each document can teach us?
2. Choose one phrase from Roosevelt's address. Quote it in a few words, then explain in your own words what it asks Congress to do and how the wording helps to persuade the listeners.
3. The lesson says that the language of the Wannsee record is dry and official, and that this is part of what makes it so chilling. Choose one phrase from the excerpt. Quote it in a few words, and explain what plain, official language does to the way a terrible plan is described. Which of the people named in the lesson, or which kinds of officials, does the document show taking part?
4. A historian wants to understand why the Holocaust happened. What can the Wannsee record show, and what can it not show? Name one other kind of evidence the historian would need, and say why it matters.
GRADING RUBRIC (16 pts)
Criteria Excellent (4) Proficient (3) Developing (2) Beginning (1)
Understanding of the material
4 pts		 Reads both sources accurately and draws on specific details from each, along with what the week's lessons taught. Reads both sources accurately but uses few specific details, or leans on only one. Shows partial understanding of one or both sources, with some errors or vague claims. Misreads the sources or does not refer to them.
Quality of reasoning
4 pts		 Connects each claim to evidence and compares the sources with care. Explains why a speaker's purpose and audience matter. Supports most claims with evidence. The comparison is sound but not fully developed. States conclusions with little support, or describes the sources without comparing them. Offers opinions without evidence from the sources.
Clarity and precision of expression
4 pts		 Writes in clear, well-organized sentences. Quotations are short, accurate, and introduced. The tone is sober and respectful. Writing is clear with minor lapses in organization or precision. Writing is often unclear or disorganized, and quotations are unclear or misplaced. Writing is too unclear to follow.
Intellectual honesty
4 pts		 Names the limits of what each source can show and says what remains uncertain without overclaiming. Acknowledges at least one limit of the evidence. Mentions limits only in passing, or claims more than the sources allow. Treats each source as complete and beyond question.
Total:
16 pts total
SUBMISSION

Answer all four questions in complete sentences. Submit your answers in the text box on the Canvas assignment page. Aim for one solid paragraph for each question. You do not need an outside source. This assignment deals with the murder of millions of people, so write with care. Your teacher will read your work and return a rubric score with a short comment.

quizzes.title: Module Intro: World War II and the Holocaust
quizzes.description:
MODULE INTRO
World War II and the Holocaust
2 questions · survey · one attempt
✹ ✦ ✹
Essential question for this week
What choices and conditions led to the Second World War and the Holocaust?
Instructions

Welcome to World War II and the Holocaust. This short check-in is not graded. Your answers help your teacher see where each student is starting, so answer honestly.

What you will be able to do

From Munich to Hiroshima: The War

  • Explain why Britain and France chose appeasement in 1938 and what followed from that choice.
  • Describe the major turning points of the war in Europe and the Pacific.
  • Evaluate which decisions by leaders, rather than larger forces alone, shaped the course of the war.

The Holocaust

  • Describe the stages by which Nazi persecution of Jews moved from discrimination to mass murder.
  • Explain how ordinary institutions and ordinary people took part in, resisted, or stood aside from the killing.
  • Explain why the Nuremberg trials and the word genocide arose from this crime.

discussions.title: Discussion: Could Britain and France Have Stopped Hitler in 1938?
discussions.html:
DISCUSSION
Could Britain and France Have Stopped Hitler in 1938?
World War II and the Holocaust
10 points · threaded discussion
✹ ✦ ✹
Before you start

Finish both lessons first. Your notes from each lesson are kept in My Notebook, the button inside the lesson, so open it before you post. Then post your answer here and reply to one classmate.

DISCUSSION PROMPT

At Munich, Chamberlain and Daladier let Hitler take the Sudetenland. The Czechs had strong mountain defenses, a modern army, and an alliance with France. Britain's army was small, its air defenses were incomplete, and the public did not want war. Some historians say war in 1938 would have found Germany weaker. Others say the delay gave Britain time to build fighter planes and radar.

Take a position. Could Britain and France have stopped Hitler in 1938? Support your position with at least two specific details from the lessons, and include one detail that points the other way. Explain why you weigh the evidence as you do.

Aim for about 150 to 200 words.

RESPOND TO A CLASSMATE

Reply to one classmate. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with a detail from the lessons that they did not use. If not, explain respectfully where it falls short, and point to a detail from the lessons that supports your view.

GRADING RUBRIC (10 pts)
Criteria Substantive (full credit) Thin (partial credit) Missing (no credit)
Claim and evidence
5 pts		 Takes a clear position, supports it with at least two specific details from the lessons, and deals fairly with a detail that points the other way. Takes a position but gives only one detail, or stays general, or ignores the opposing detail. No post, or no clear position.
Response to a classmate
5 pts		 Answers a specific point in a classmate's post and either strengthens it with a new detail or explains politely where it falls short. Replies in general terms, such as agreeing or disagreeing without a detail from the lessons. No reply.
10 pts total
